question: A ring-shaped metallic sheet has outer and inner radii 10 cm and 6 cm. What percentage of the full circle's area is the ring?
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

The percentage area of a ring relative to the full circle is independent of π.

Required Percentage = [(R² − r²) ÷ R²] × 100

⇒ Required Percentage = [(10² − 6²) ÷ 10²] × 100

⇒ Required Percentage = [(100 − 36) ÷ 100] × 100 = 64%

**∴ The correct answer is 64%.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

 
 
 
 
• 
 r = 6 cm
 
• 
 R = 10 cm
 Metallic Ring Area

**Given:**

Outer radius of the metallic sheet (R) = 10 cm

Inner radius of the metallic sheet (r) = 6 cm

**Formula Used:**

Area of a circle = π × R²

Area of the ring = Area of outer circle − Area of inner circle

**Calculation:**

⇒ Area of the full outer circle = π × 10² = 100π cm²

⇒ Area of the inner empty circle = π × 6² = 36π cm²

⇒ Area of the ring = 100π − 36π = 64π cm²

⇒ Percentage of the full circle's area = (Area of ring ÷ Area of full circle) × 100

⇒ Percentage = (64π ÷ 100π) × 100

⇒ Percentage = 64%

**∴ The correct answer is 64%.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Concentric Circles

Two or more circles that share the exact same center point but have different radii are called concentric circles.

Area of an Annulus (Ring)

The flat shape bounded by two concentric circles is known as an annulus. Its area is calculated using the formula π(R² − r²).

Width of the Ring

The uniform width or thickness of any circular ring is strictly the difference between the outer radius and the inner radius: Width = R − r.
